To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the variational approach is a very powerful tool to study theN-body system interacting with scalar and/or vector mesons, that theN-body system is stable forN=3 andN=4, that theN=3 and N=4 systems are stable with respect to the addition of a single particle and that theN=5 system has a stable ground state with respect to the exchange of two particles.
the binding of theN-body meson-nucleon system is due to the self-energy terms of the particles, while the exchange terms give rise to the saturation of the nuclear system.
the variational approach to a system of non-relativistic fermions interacting with scalar and pseudoscalar mesons is able to reproduce the properties of a nuclear medium.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of how to describe the properties of a system ofN nucleons interacting through the exchange of mesons, without resorting to the perturbation expansion.
the problem of the interaction of a system ofN nucleons and their meson cloud, in which the mesons are treated as dynamical variables.
the nonperturbative treatment, in the framework of the path integral approach, ofN interacting non-relativistic fermions in the presence of scalar and vector meson fields.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the meson theory of nuclear binding is a viable alternative to the nucleon-nucleon interaction.
a variational treatment of a system ofN nucleons interacting through mesons leads to a binding of the system and to a saturation of the energy per particle.
a non-perturbative treatment ofN-body systems with dynamical meson fields is possible and that the variational approach is an efficient tool in this respect.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the variational method, in conjunction with the path-integral formulation of the theory, provides a powerful tool in the study ofN-body systems with dynamical meson fields.
theN-body system is stable and the binding energy increases with the number of particles.
theN-body system is bound by the exchange of vector mesons, while scalar mesons contribute to the binding through self energy terms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the variational approach is a powerful tool in the nonperturbative treatment forN-body systems.
the variational approach is an effective method to treat theN-body system, and that theN-body system can be treated non-perturbatively.

a non-perturbative approach to the problem of the N-body system interacting with mesons is possible, and that the variational calculation of theN-body action provides a useful tool to investigate the structure of the system.
